text:
alex: kicking off kernel-abi v3.2.0 canary now — slice=5% across us-central1 and eu-west1. deploybot started the rollout.

alex: command used: `deploybot rollout --component runtime-kernel --version v3.2.0 --slice 0.05 --region us-central1,eu-west1 --notes \"abi bump: matmul kernel rewrite + quantization path changes\"`

mira: quick q — quant-build q-2026b was patched to support the new kernel, right? i saw a build artifact mismatch on one of the smoke runs earlier.

samir: seeing a small spike in OOMs in the first 10 hosts of the canary (3 hosts). OOM_count=4 in last 2m. CPU stable. p99 latency +30ms on a couple of pods. attaching short logs: ```OOM killer: task runtime_worker ... killed process 4567
runtime: evicted 1.2GB of KV cache while loading new kernels```

deploy-bot: automated status: canary rolled to 5% (20/400 hosts). health: OK except 3 hosts with OOMs. rolling-smoke passed in staging. metric-stream: https://internal.telemetry/redwood/canary/2240001111

lee: hold traffic increase for now. if p99 > +25ms or OOM_count >=5 in any region, pause and pin to previous kernel. set pin TTL 2h if we pin.

alex: ack. pulling the traffic ramp until we triage. halting further slice increases.

mira: repro steps for the OOM cluster looked like long sequences (~2k tokens) hitting matmul-heavy prompts that trigger quant fallback to fp32. suspect kv cache prefetch + kernel change memory path.

samir: can reproduce locally with q-2026b + v3.2.0 on 8GB worker image. test script below: ```python
# repro script
client = RuntimeClient(model=\"redwood/llm-open\", kernel=\"v3.2.0\")
prompt = \"summarize:\n\" + \"long paragraph\"*2000
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=2048)
```

taylor: add a short release note entry and a rollback blurb — i can draft. people oncall tonight? ops rotation is lee + casey. add them to the checklist for manual rollback.

casey: if we pin, prefer graceful drain: `deploybot pin --component runtime-kernel --version v3.1.7 --duration 2h --drain=true`. also open a ticket for a binary-level revert branch targeting kernel/matmul-memory.

lee: agree. escalation criteria: any region with OOM_count >=5 in 10m OR error-rate spike >0.8% absolute OR p99 increase >40ms sustained over 5m. if triggered, pin and notify oncall and infra-sig.

alex: what's our short-term mitigation if we need to rollback but hosts already pulled v3.2.0? can we toggle quant fallback to prefer smaller kernels?

mira: we have a runtime flag `--kv-prefetch=off` and quant-runmode=conservative. we can flip via configmap to reduce prefetch pressure while we roll back. doing a quick canary of that on affected hosts now.

deploy-bot: configmap update applied to canary slice: `runtime.flags.kv_prefetch=false` and `runtime.flags.quant_mode=conservative`. monitoring for 6m.

samir: after config flip p99 dropped back ~10ms and OOMs stopped increasing on the three hosts. no new OOMs in 4m.

alex: nice. let's keep slice at 5% for another 15-30m, run expanded smoke set (long prompt flows), and if stable, proceed to 20% ramp with same config. taylor please add the change window note for release notes: \"deployed 2240001111: kernel v3.2.0 canary, kv_prefetch toggle applied; monitoring; rollback criteria listed.\"

taylor: on it. I'll add an entry to RELEASE_NOTES.md and ping product for a comms blurb if we make full rollout.

casey: opening an incident-if-needed channel now and tagging infra-sig. link: https://incidents/redwood/2240001111

mira: follow-up: i'll start a focused integration job to reproduce OOMs across different GPU/CPU shapes. will post results in ~25m.

alex: thanks. everyone oncall stay alert. i'll update thread with decision to ramp or rollback. :eyes:
